title: AnomalyJev: Towards Evaluating Image Anomaly Explanations via Claim-Level Verification
abstract: arXiv:2610.27565v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Recent multimodal LLM (MLLM)-based anomaly detection (AD) methods can generate textual explanations that help interpret their predictions. However, reliably and efficiently evaluating these explanations remains challenging. While LLM judges can assess explanations through structured rubrics, they often require substantial token generation, making evaluation costly and difficult to scale. We instead propose to anchor evaluation in the available ground truth by extracting verifiable claims from each explanation and verifying them against the corresponding annotations. We instantiate this idea as AnomalyJev, a lightweight framework that extracts verifiable claims from contextualised representations using ground-truth-defined queries and pointer based heads, without token generation. translated_title: AnomalyJev：基于断言级验证的图像异常解释评估方法
translated_abstract: 近期基于多模态大语言模型（MLLM）的异常检测（AD）方法能够生成有助于解释其预测结果的文本说明。然而，如何可靠且高效地评估这些说明仍然是一个挑战。虽然使用大语言模型（LLM）作为评审员可以通过结构化评分标准来评估说明，但这种方式通常需要生成大量的token，导致评估成本高昂且难以扩展。为此，我们提出将评估锚定在已有的真实标注上，从每个说明中提取可验证的断言，并将其与对应的标注进行比对验证。我们将这一想法实现为AnomalyJev，这是一个轻量级框架，利用由真实标注定义的查询和基于指针的输出头，从上下文化表示中提取可验证的断言，而无需生成token。随后将这些断言与真实标注进行验证，以评分解释的忠实度和完整性。为了进行评估，我们构建了一个包含640条人工标注说明的数据集……（原文摘要至此被截断）
tldr: 提出AnomalyJev，一个无需token生成的轻量级评估框架，通过从图像异常检测模型生成的文本解释中提取可验证断言并与真实标注比对验证，从而高效且可靠地评估解释的忠实度与完整性。
en_tdlr: AnomalyJev is a lightweight, token-generation-free framework that evaluates image anomaly explanations by extracting verifiable claims from contextualized representations and verifying them against ground-truth annotations to score faithfulness and completeness.
